outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Text‑to‑Image Diffusion and the Need for Controlled Finetuning
outline.description: Sets the stage by reviewing modern text‑to‑image diffusion models, their strengths, and why downstream control (subject‑driven and conditional generation) is challenging. Introduces the desiderata for a good finetuning method.
subtopics: Overview of recent text‑to‑image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, DALL‑E 2, Imagen, etc.)
Limitations of plain text prompting for fine‑grained control
Two key downstream tasks: subject‑driven generation and controllable generation
Desired properties of finetuning: efficiency and preservation of pretrained generative ability
Existing finetuning strategies (small‑LR updates, LoRA, adapters) and their shortcomings

outline.chapter_title: Geometric Perspective on Neural Representations: Hyperspherical Energy
outline.description: Introduces hyperspherical energy as a structural measure of neuron relationships, explains why angular information is crucial for semantics, and motivates its use as a preservation metric during finetuning.
subtopics: Definition of hyperspherical energy (HE) and pairwise cosine similarity
Intuition: angles encode semantic information (SphereNet, cosine‑based representations)
Toy experiment illustrating angular vs. magnitude information in autoencoders
Why Euclidean distance between weights is insufficient as preservation metric
Properties of HE: invariance under orthogonal transformations

outline.description: Derives the core idea of OFT – learning a layer‑wise orthogonal matrix that rotates pretrained weights, thereby keeping HE unchanged. Formalizes the optimization problem.
subtopics: Problem statement: finetuning as constrained optimization
Derivation of HE preservation condition → orthogonal transformation
Mathematical formulation: \(W = R W^0\) with \(R^T R = I\)
Interpretation as rotating the canonical coordinate system of neurons
Comparison with additive low‑rank updates (LoRA) and plain gradient descent

outline.description: Presents practical ways to represent and learn orthogonal matrices at scale, including Cayley transform, block‑diagonal decomposition, and parameter sharing.
subtopics: Cayley transform: constructing orthogonal matrices from skew‑symmetric Q
Block‑diagonal orthogonal matrices to reduce O(d²) parameters to O(d²/r)
Parameter sharing across blocks for further reduction to O(d²/r²)
(Optional) Comparison of parameter counts with LoRA and full‑matrix updates
Implementation details: ensuring numerical stability, initializing R = I

outline.chapter_title: Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT) – Adding a Radius Constraint
outline.description: Extends OFT by limiting how far the orthogonal matrix can deviate from the identity, giving a tighter control over model drift.
subtopics: "ε‑ball" constraint: \(\|R - I\| \le ε\)
Embedding the constraint into the Cayley parameterization via Q and projected gradient descent
Effect of ε on flexibility vs. stability (illustrative plots)
Practical guidelines for choosing ε in different downstream tasks

outline.:description: Adds an optional diagonal scaling matrix D to OFT while keeping HE unchanged, increasing expressive power with negligible extra cost.
:subtopics: Motivation: magnitude can adjust feature strength without affecting angles
(R W⁰ D)ᵀx formulation
Training dynamics when both R and D are learned
Empirical impact on performance (summary of appendix results)

outline.,chapter_title: Applying OFT to Text‑to‑Image Diffusion Architectures
outline.:description: Shows how OFT integrates into typical diffusion pipelines (UNet backbone, attention layers, convolutional blocks). Discusses architecture‑agnostic nature.
:subtopics: $\.R$ insertion points: linear layers, QKV projections in attention, conv kernels
$\.R$ sharing strategies across layers vs. per‑layer matrices
$\.R$ block structure for convolutional channels (depthwise interpretation)
$\.R$ comparison with ControlNet adapters in terms of inference cost

outline.:description: Detailed walkthrough of adapting OFU/COFT for few‑shot subject personalization. Covers training setup, loss functions, and evaluation metrics.
:subtopics: "DreamBooth" pipeline recap (class prior loss, reconstruction loss)
$ \.R$ finetuning only the cross‑attention layers (as in LoRA baseline)
$ \.R$ hyperparameters: block count r, ε for COFT, learning rate schedule
$ \.R$ Quantitative metrics: DINO similarity, CLIP-I/T, LPIPS diversity
$ \.R$ Qualitative analysis: identity preservation vs. prompt fidelity

outline.:description: Adapts OFT to image‑to‑image style tasks where an extra control signal is provided. Explains task formulations Canny→image, segmentation→image, landmarks→face.
:subtopics: $ \.R$ integration with conditioning modules (concatenated control embeddings)
$ \.R$ Training dataset preparation for each control modality
$ \.R$ New control consistency metrics (IoU/F1 for edges, mean IoU/accuracy for segmentation, ℓ₂ landmark error)
$ \.R$ Comparison of convergence speed against ControlNet/T2I‑Adapter/LoRA

outline.:description: Summarizes key empirical findings across both tasks. Highlights faster convergence, stability, sample efficiency and lack of inference overhead.
:subtopics: "Finetuning stability" plots and discussion (iterations vs. quality)
"Convergence speed" graphs showing COFT/OFT beating baselines after few epochs
"Ablation studies": effect of block size r, ε value, re‑scaled OFT vs. vanilla OFT
"Parameter efficiency" comparison tables (trainable params vs. performance)
"Human evaluation" methodology and outcomes

outline.,chapter_title: Theoretical Insights and Connections to Related Work
outline.:description: Places OFT within the broader literature on model adaptation and representation geometry.
:subtopics: "Relation to LoRA": low‑rank additive vs. full‑rank orthogonal multiplicative updates
"Orthogonal over‑parameterized training" – similarities & differences in objective (preserve vs. minimize HE)
"Why orthogonal transforms improve optimization landscape on hypersphere manifolds"
"Limitations of minimizing HE for finetuning"

outline.:description: Provides a cookbook for researchers/practitioners who want to apply OFT/COFT to new diffusion models or other vision tasks.
:subtopics: "Choosing the block number r" based on layer width and GPU memory
"Setting ε for COFT": tradeoffs per task type
"Efficient computation of Cayley transform" – avoiding full matrix inversion via series or approximations
"Training tricks": warm‑up learning rates, gradient clipping, checkpointing orthogonal matrices

outline.:description: Discusses unresolved challenges identified by the authors and potential research avenues.
:subtopics: "Scalable orthogonal parametrization without matrix inverses"
"Compositionality of multiple orthogonal transforms for multi‑task learning"
"Better parameter‐efficient structures beyond block diagonal"
"Extending OFT to other modalities (video diffusion, speech synthesis)"
